correctness.rationale: For every fixed-\(p\) LEFT step, the previous-gradient Rayleigh quotient lies in \([\mu,L]\), hence the actual step length \(h=p/r\) puts every modal product \(h\lambda\) in \([p/\kappa,p\kappa]\). For \(p\ge1\), the largest absolute modal multiplier is at most \(p\kappa-1\), which yields the squared-gradient and objective-gap bounds. The explicit two-dimensional warm-up gives \(g_1\) with squared endpoint-component ratio \(1/\varepsilon\) and \(h_1\to p/\mu\), so both ratios tend to \((p\kappa-1)^2\). Thus the factor and the frontier \(p\kappa\le2\) are exact.

value.rationale: The source promotes a longer-than-BB1 step and interprets \(p\in[1.5,2)\) as a stable regime, while also observing that larger \(p\) slows asymptotic convergence and motivating spectral truncation. The sharp law \((p\kappa-1)^2\) exposes the complementary finite-horizon cost: increasing \(p\) contracts the exact universal monotonicity window from \(\kappa\le2\) at BB1 to \(\kappa\le2/p\). This is a natural parameter-safety boundary for the method, not an arbitrary scalar exercise, and it explains why local asymptotic stability can coexist with very large early spikes.
